OpenSpec: agree on the change before the code

The problem it solves

Give an agent a big request and it will build something plausible, which is not always what I meant. The intent lives in a chat that vanishes, so a week later nobody knows why the code looks the way it does, and the next session starts the argument again.

The general idea

OpenSpec is spec-driven development in plain files. Every change gets its own folder with a proposal.md (what and why), a design.md (how) and a tasks.md (the steps). The agent implements the tasks, and when the change is done it is archived: the spec deltas merge into specs/, which stays as the current description of the system. OpenSpec does not call a model itself. It manages the files, and my agent does the writing and the coding.

Examples

openspec/
  specs/                 # what the system does today
  changes/
    add-dark-mode/
      proposal.md        # what and why
      design.md          # how
      tasks.md           # - [ ] steps the agent ticks off

The workflow in commands:

openspec new change "add-dark-mode"
openspec status --change "add-dark-mode"
openspec list
# in the agent: propose, explore, apply, update, sync, archive

Tips from my setup

  • One skill per step. Propose, explore, apply, update, sync and archive each have a skill, so a whole change is a few short commands in the agent.
  • Explore before proposing. The explore step is a thinking partner: I describe the problem, it investigates the code and asks questions, and nothing is written yet.
  • A cheap worker for the paperwork. Exploring and generating the artifacts run on a small Haiku agent, and the stronger model implements the tasks.
  • Visible in herdr. A herdr plugin shows the active change of each project in the sidebar, and one key opens a browser of the changes. See the post about herdr.
  • Keep changes small. One change, one folder, a handful of tasks. The herdr-pomodoro plugin was built like this, one archived change at a time.
